newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK 97 FX POLICY WILL REMAIN ANTI-INFLATIONARY - BOG.
newsitem.headline: GREEK 97 FX POLICY WILL REMAIN ANTI-INFLATIONARY - BOG.

text.p: Greece's foreign exchange policy will continue to be anti-inflationary in 1997 but the conduct of its policy will be more flexible, central bank governor Lucas Papademos told reporters.
"The forex policy will remain anti-inflationary," said Papademos. "Of course, the conduct of foreign exchange policy in 1997 will be more flexible."
When asked whether a faster deceleration of inflation would lead to a higher ecu/drachma level than would have been the case otherwise, Papademos told Reuters: "Possibly."
The drachma slid by 1.0 percent against the ecu in 1996 and 3.0 percent in 1995, in line with the central bank's pre-announced targets.
Papademos declined to confirm or deny a report in today's financial daily Imerisia that the central bank would announce no volatility traget for the drachma in 1997.
